content.user_title: Build Python Code Nodes for n8n
content.value_statement: n8n Python Code nodes have strict data access, return format, and library limits. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to write correct transformations.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to choose Python, JavaScript, or other n8n nodes.
Shows correct _input, _json, _node, _items, and _item data access patterns.
Documents the required list return format with a json item wrapper.
Provides patterns for filtering, aggregation, validation, regex, statistics, and dates.
Lists supported standard library modules and unavailable external packages.
Highlights common errors such as webhook body nesting and KeyError prevention.
limitations: It does not execute workflows or validate a live n8n instance.
It cannot enable external Python packages in n8n Code nodes.
It focuses on Python Code nodes, not full workflow design.
Some linked companion files are referenced but not present in this package.

use_cases.title: Create batch transformations
use_cases.description: Build Python Code node logic that processes all input items and returns consistent n8n items.

use_cases.title: Fix webhook parsing
use_cases.description: Use body nesting guidance to read webhook fields and avoid missing-key errors.

use_cases.title: Choose the right node type
use_cases.description: Decide when Python, JavaScript, Set, Filter, IF, or HTTP Request nodes are better choices.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic transformation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to write a Python Code node that reads all items, adds a processed flag, and returns valid n8n items.

prompt_templates.title: Handle webhook data safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to write Python for a webhook payload. Read fields from the body object and use safe defaults.

prompt_templates.title: Aggregate and validate records
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a Python Code node that filters invalid records, calculates totals, and returns a summary plus errors.

prompt_templates.title: Review a complex Code node
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to audit my Python Code node for mode selection, return format, data access, unavailable imports, and safer alternatives.

output_examples.input: User asks for a Python Code node that calculates totals from multiple order items.
output_examples.output: The assistant returns a Run Once for All Items approach, explains the required item wrapper, and notes empty-input handling.

output_examples.input: User has webhook fields that work in other nodes but fail in Python.
output_examples.output: The assistant identifies body nesting, recommends safe dictionary access, and describes how to return the corrected fields.

output_examples.input: User wants to import requests in a Python Code node.
output_examples.output: The assistant explains the package limit and recommends an HTTP Request node or JavaScript helper instead.

best_practices: Use Python only when its standard library or syntax is the best fit.
Return the n8n item structure on every code path.
Prefer safe dictionary access and explicit defaults for optional fields.
anti_patterns: Importing external packages such as requests, pandas, or numpy in a Python Code node.
Reading webhook fields directly from the root object when they are under body.
Using Python Code nodes for simple mapping or filtering that native n8n nodes handle.

faq.question: Does this skill run Python code?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples for Python Code nodes in n8n.

faq.question: Can I use external packages with this skill?
faq.answer: No. The skill documents that n8n Python Code nodes support standard library modules only.

faq.question: Which n8n Python modes does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers Python Beta and Native modes, including their different data access variables.

faq.question: Should I use Python or JavaScript in n8n?
faq.answer: Use JavaScript for most Code nodes. Use Python when standard library features or Python syntax are needed.

faq.question: Does it help with webhook data?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains that webhook fields are nested under the body object in Python Code nodes.

faq.question: Can it validate my workflow?
faq.answer: It can guide manual checks, but it does not connect to n8n or run validation.
